bind_semantics: Example is an idempotent explicit bind to the already-bound current verified target: no registry mutation and unchanged revision.
Only existing profile/source UUID rows of the same provider and parent are admitted. Missing IDs require separate explicit registry import/create policy; bind never invents identities.

Require exact runtime, captured binding revision and current opaque target, then resolve both private registry owners/selectors on player. Wire callers cannot supply selectors, grants or owner fields.

Binding source and parent to a different target is NOT implemented by this packet: refuse until a host atomic-or-honest-partial multi-row binding policy is qualified. Never claim registry.bind(source) also changes its parent.
Read back the actual registry and re-resolve before acknowledging. Conflict/unknown is not success and is not retried.
Targets and bindingcatalog are player projections: Control consumes this exact shape and never derives private bindings from registry public rows.
projection_rules: Join each public source row to its profile_id profile row; require same provider and both actual private registry.resolve owners/selectors to match the current verified target. Do not pass registry.list().entries directly as wire bindings.

A wire binding is exactly {scope,target_id,codecVersion}; scope carries profile/source UUIDs and provider. Its binding_revision is the outer registry revision encoded as a string. Private selectors/owner data are never returned.

target_id is an opaque runtime-owned association, not a slot, display name, playlist URL, configuration hash or a persistent identity. Only the active verified target is enumerated in this first scope.
The bindings/target projection is not yet registered; Control must not infer or implement an alternative projection. Bindingcatalog/bind remain separate from the frozen seven transfer operations.
unsupported: Foreign paired PMS without explicit rebinding
Empty list collections or present defaults other than the retained generated Favorites default (including null)
Arbitrary unportable legacy strings, negative/unsafe legacy numbers or unsupported reference codecs
Uninitialized or isolated-context media/favorites runtime; inspection never initializes, migrates or writes legacy claims
The first document carries canonical Plex locators and optional title snapshots; it does not assert full folder ancestry or physical file paths

persistence_and_retention.restart_status: Fresh read-only same-scope grant/binding authorization plus actual favorites-store readback; no old runtime write-ticket revival.

limit_notes: No current runtime advertises this object. All modules, exact storage/key codecs, explicit binding authorization and trusted fresh-operation/budget admission must be integrated and qualified first.
Persistent means actual adapter persisted readback, not filesystem fsync or cross-store atomicity. Cookie-backed stores are admitted only when every required readback succeeds.
Limits intersect: byte/node/plan/ledger limits can refuse a collection below its per-list item ceiling; admission never raises caps or evicts uncertain receipts.
schema_decision_remaining: Approved current-only idempotent-existing-binding policy; no creation or different-target rebinding in first packet. Runtime registration remains absent.
